claim: For a game that XORs figures, toggling the overlay on every plot keeps it exact through erase, draw and redraw with no place list.

evidence.text: Each plot is repeated on the Layer 2 overlay by toggling (255 <-> 7), so the overlay is the XOR of what the game has plotted, without storing any figure's place; a game that XORs figures needs no place list.
evidence.quote: A game that XORs figures needs no place list: toggling on the overlay keeps it exact through every erase, draw and redraw.

evidence.text: Balls take a sprite per call where the call says; erasing calls name the place they already are; follow every call with the sprite.
evidence.quote: Balls: slots 118-121, patterns 124-127, a sprite per call where the call says; erasing calls name the place it already is.

evidence.text: Converted writes go to a 1-bit shadow screen, so ULA XOR shadow == the original screen at every moment (XOR is linear); on one shared XOR layer Dizzy and the grease gun cancelled each other's pixels (hardware test).
